title: Higgsfield Katana vs Genjutsu: What Each Does, Price and Speed (2026)
html:
Higgsfield now sells two ways to remake a video with AI. They sound alike and do different jobs. Genjutsu edits one clip. Katana rebuilds a whole edit.

The short answer: use Genjutsu to swap a person, outfit, product or place inside one clip while the camera move and timing stay as filmed. Use Katana to rebuild a multi-shot reference edit around your own people or products. Both spend the credits of a Higgsfield plan. If you would rather pay per clip, Riftn Maboroshi does both jobs with no subscription.

Katana vs Genjutsu at a glance

  • What it does: Genjutsu edits one clip, by Object Swap or Motion Transfer. Katana rebuilds a full edit from a reference video or a preset.
  • Where it runs: Genjutsu on higgsfield.ai. Katana inside an AI chat assistant, through Higgsfield's connector.
  • Input video: Genjutsu takes one clip of 4 to 30 seconds. Katana takes your own reference video or a preset from its library.
  • Your images: Genjutsu takes up to 30 reference images. Katana takes up to five photos of people, products or clothing.
  • Output: Genjutsu goes up to 1080p. Katana follows the reference's length, aspect ratio and frame rate.
  • Price: Genjutsu costs 40 to 144 credits for 15 seconds. Katana shows the exact credit cost before each run.
  • Plan needed: both spend Higgsfield plan credits. Katana needs an active Higgsfield subscription.

What Genjutsu does

Genjutsu takes a real video and changes one thing in it. It has two modes:

  • Object Swap: replace a character, outfit, product, location or object, and keep the rest of the shot.
  • Motion Transfer: keep the motion, camera and timing, and rebuild the scene from your references.

You upload one clip of 4 to 30 seconds, add up to 30 reference images, and pick a preset or write a short description. Output goes up to 1080p.

In October 2026 Higgsfield added Genjutsu Lite, a faster option that costs about a third as much. It takes up to 10 reference images, outputs 720p or 1080p, and applies changes automatically with no mode choice.

What Katana does

Katana is an editing skill that runs inside an AI chat. You give it a reference edit, either your own video or a preset from its library, plus up to five photos of people, products or clothing. It rebuilds the video with your assets, keeping the reference's shots and pacing.

You correct it in plain words. Katana re-renders only the shots you change, and corrections that only reassemble existing shots cost nothing. The finished clip appears in the chat and in your Higgsfield assets.

The two tools share one account. A clip made with Genjutsu can become a Katana reference, and a Katana edit can be taken further.

Genjutsu price

Higgsfield's own figures for a 15-second clip, checked September 2026:

  • 480p: 40 credits, about $2.00
  • 720p: 104 credits, about $5.20
  • 1080p: 144 credits, about $7.20

Object Swap and Motion Transfer cost the same. Genjutsu Lite costs about one third of these.

Katana price

Katana uses the credits of your existing Higgsfield plan, with no separate fee. The chat shows the exact credit cost before each generation. Higgsfield does not publish a fixed Katana price, because the cost depends on the edit.

How long do Genjutsu and Katana take?

Higgsfield does not publish render times for either tool. As a guide, its own measurements put an 8-second 720p clip at about 1.5 to 4 minutes on the video models it hosts, and 1080p takes longer than 720p. Genjutsu Lite is the faster Genjutsu option.

What model does Genjutsu use?

Higgsfield does not say which models run under Genjutsu or Katana. Genjutsu-style editing is usually a chain of steps: depth, a mask around the subject, a face mesh, a video model that re-renders the subject, and the original audio put back at the end. We take that chain apart step by step in how Genjutsu works.

Which one should you use?

  • Swap one thing in one clip: Genjutsu.
  • Swap something fast and cheap: Genjutsu Lite.
  • Rebuild a whole edit with your product or cast: Katana.

A per-clip alternative: Riftn Maboroshi

Maboroshi, inside Riftn Creator, covers both jobs without a subscription:

  • Subject swap, like Genjutsu: a 15-second clip costs $4.55 on the Kling route, with the original audio put back untouched.
  • Multi-shot rebuild, like Katana: Remake splits a clip into up to eight shots, lets you redo any single shot, and stitches them back with the original audio.
  • You see the price in dollars first, and the quote is the charge.

Full prices and the honest cases where Higgsfield is cheaper are in our Higgsfield Genjutsu alternative guide.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between Higgsfield Katana and Genjutsu?

Genjutsu changes one thing inside a single clip. Katana rebuilds a whole multi-shot edit around your photos, inside an AI chat.

How much does Genjutsu cost?

About $2.00, $5.20 or $7.20 for a 15-second clip at 480p, 720p or 1080p, paid in Higgsfield credits. Genjutsu Lite costs about a third as much.

How long does Genjutsu take?

Higgsfield does not publish a time. The video models it hosts take about 1.5 to 4 minutes for a short 720p clip, and 1080p takes longer.

What model does Genjutsu use?

Higgsfield does not name it. Our guide to how Genjutsu works shows the open models behind the same effect.

Do I need a subscription for Katana?

Yes. Katana needs an active Higgsfield subscription and spends its credits. Riftn Maboroshi charges per clip instead.

Riftn is a social media protocol with a full AI studio built in. Try Maboroshi.

Higgsfield figures come from Higgsfield's Genjutsu, Katana and generation-time articles as checked in November 2026. Higgsfield changes its plans often, so check its live pricing before you compare.
